content:
Yesterday we saw that the three burnt offering animals; the young bull, the ram, and the one-year-old lamb - together point to Christ’s sacrifice covering all three ages of God’s plan: the world that was, the world that is, and the world that is to come. And we saw that the total number of burnt offering animals across all twelve leaders was 36, and that 36 appears in Joshua 7:5 in connection with broken covenant and the judgment that follows. Today we look at the second time 36 appears in Scripture, and then we bring both together to see what the thirty-six burnt offerings in Numbers 7 are truly saying.

The second appearance of 36 as a significant number is found in 2 Chronicles 16:1:
“In the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah.” Asa was the great-grandson of David and one of the better kings of Judah. He did not begin badly. In fact, he began remarkably well. In the early years of his reign, Asa removed the idols from the land, broke down the pagan altars, commanded all of Judah to seek Yahweh sincerely, and restored proper worship at the temple.

2 Chronicles 14:2 says plainly: “Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of Yahweh his God.” This was not a half-hearted king. This was a man who had a genuine beginning with Yahweh.

The clearest proof of his early faith is in 2 Chronicles 14:11, when a massive Ethiopian army came against Judah with a 10 Lakh soldiers and 300 chariots. Against overwhelming odds, Asa did not reach for military alliances or clever strategy. He cried to Yahweh directly: “Yahweh, there is no one besides You to help, whether the powerful or those who have no strength. Help us, Yahweh our God, for we rely on You, and in Your name we have come against this multitude.” And Yahweh gave him a complete and miraculous victory. This was a man who knew what it meant to depend on God alone.

But something shifted. Slowly, quietly, in the years that followed, the dependence that had made Asa’s faith so real began to thin. By the thirty-sixth year of his reign, when a new threat came from Baasha king of Israel, Asa did not turn to Yahweh as he had before. Instead, he took silver and gold from the house of Yahweh and sent it to Ben-Hadad king of Syria to buy a military alliance. The plan worked outwardly. The threat from Baasha was removed. But the prophet Hanani came to Asa and delivered a word that cut to the heart of what had happened: “Because you relied on the king of Syria, and did not rely on Yahweh your God, the army of the king of Syria has escaped you” (2 Chronicles 16:7). You used to rely on Yahweh. Now you rely on Syria. The reliance had shifted.

Asa’s response to the rebuke reveals how far he had drifted. He did not humble himself. He did not repent. He was angry, and he threw the prophet into prison. Later, when Asa became diseased in his feet, 2 Chronicles 16:12 records the painful truth: “In his disease he sought not Yahweh, but to the physicians.” The problem was not the physicians. The problem was that Asa no longer sought Yahweh first. The man who had once cried to God against 10 lakh soldiers now could not bring himself to seek Yahweh in a personal illness. He died after forty-one years of reign, and the thirty-sixth year became the turning point that the rest of his life never recovered from.

Now we can see both incidents together. Thirty-six men died in Joshua 7 because Achan secretly broke the covenant and chapter 7 begins by saying “​But Israel violated the instructions”. The thirty-sixth year of Asa saw a faithful king quietly shift his trust from Yahweh to human alliances. In both cases, the issue is not open, dramatic, outward rebellion. In both cases it is the slow drift, the hidden compromise, the subtle move from dependence on Yahweh toward dependence on human strength.
Thirty-six is the number of the broken covenant; not the spectacular breaking, but the quiet one. Not the man who walks away all at once, but the man who walks a little further from the altar each year until one day he no longer goes there at all.

And into this number, Christ steps. The twelve tribal leaders brought thirty-six burnt offerings to the altar of dedication. Thirty-six animals, wholly consumed, ascending entirely before Yahweh. The number of broken covenant was placed on the altar, and in its place Christ’s complete obedience ascended as a pleasing aroma. Romans 5:19 says: “For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the one man’s obedience the many will be made righteous.” Adam broke the covenant. Achan broke it secretly. Asa broke it slowly. And every person since has added their own breaking to the total. But Christ reversed the disobedience of Adam and every Asa and every Achan with a single complete, total, utterly surrendered obedience. The thirty-six burnt offerings ascending to Yahweh over twelve days are saying: the broken covenant is being answered. The gap is being closed. The obedience is being offered that covers every form of the breaking.

The lesson of Asa is not a comfortable one for those who have been walking with God for many years. It is not an incident about a man who never knew Yahweh. It is a story about a man who knew Him very well, who had experienced miraculous deliverance, who had a genuine and public beginning of faith; and who slowly drifted in the thirty-sixth year. The warning is not for beginners. It is for us. It is for those who have been serving for many years and have stopped noticing that the reliance has shifted; that the instinct to cry to Yahweh first has slowly given way to the instinct to reach out to Human help.

Hebrews 3:12-13 says: “Take care, brothers, lest there be in any of you an evil, unbelieving heart, leading you to fall away from the living God. But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today, that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.” The deceitfulness of sin is exactly what the number 36 warns about. It is not the dramatic fall. It is the daily, small, quiet movement of trust away from Yahweh toward human strength. Every day a little further from the altar. Every week the prayer a little shorter. Every difficulty met a little more by planning and a little less by seeking. Until one day, in the thirty-sixth year, the prophet comes and says: you used to rely on Yahweh.

The thirty-six burnt offerings of Numbers 7 were placed on the altar of dedication so that all thirty-six could ascend before Yahweh. The number of broken covenant was consecrated to God and consumed by fire. This is what Christ does in us as new creation believers. He does not just cover our past breaking of the covenant. He daily re-consecrates us, re-calls us to the altar, re-invites us to Him before the drift becomes a distance. Every morning we are invited to place ourselves on the altar again and let it be consumed by the fire of obedience and grace.

title: Prayer
text:
Yahweh, you are righteous in all Your ways and kind in all Your works (Psalm 145:17). We come before You today with the full weight of every covenant broken, every small drift away from wholehearted dependence, every Asa-year in our own lives when we reached for the human alliance instead of crying to You. We thank You that Christ stepped into the number 36 and reversed it with His complete, total, unbroken obedience. We thank You that His thirty-six burnt offerings ascended before you as a sweet aroma, covering every form of the breaking. Search us today for the quiet shift; the places where trust has slowly moved from You to human strength,
the places where the instinct to seek You first has grown duller than it once was.
Bring us back to the altar. help us never to become the Asa who had a miraculous beginning, but whose thirty-sixth year became his downfall. Keep us wholehearted until the end. In Christ’s name, amen.
